requirements.statement: The importer chooses the country the plants or wood originate from, from a list of countries. It is required: a notification cannot be completed without it. This is the country of origin, not the country the consignment is dispatched from, which is a separate datum even though IPAFFS labels both 'Country of origin'.
requirements.why: Policy names the country of origin as data needed for risk assessment and inspection planning, and IPAFFS captures it as a mandatory single choice. Backed by both sources.

requirements.statement: The country of origin is asked on its own page, captioned 'About the consignment' with the heading 'Origin of the plants, plant product or other objects'. The question is the whole page: no hint and no body copy. The page has one button, 'Save and continue'. The browser tab title matches the heading, unlike IPAFFS, where the mismatched title is a defect.
requirements.why: IPAFFS is the only source for how the question is asked; the policy is silent on presentation. The title mismatch is recorded by the trace itself as a defect, so it is not carried forward.

requirements.statement: Continuing without choosing a country of origin shows an error and keeps the importer on the page.
requirements.why: Follows from the country being required (req-001). The wording is an open question with a default.

requirements.statement: Wherever the notification's answers are shown back, the country of origin is shown by its name (for example 'Austria'), not its code.
requirements.why: IPAFFS behaviour; plain English for the reader. Policy is silent.

requirements.statement: The country of origin is asked before the commodity details: after the importer has chosen the import type, and before the commodity code and the genus and species.
requirements.why: IPAFFS page order. The country is the notification's first 'where from' answer and the commodity questions follow it.

requirements.statement: For each commodity line the importer gives the commodity code of the goods.
requirements.why: Policy requires the commodity code; the goal names it. The trace slice does not cover the commodity code question itself, only that it comes before the genus-and-species pick in IPAFFS, so the requirement rests on policy alone for what and on the trace for where.

requirements.statement: For each commodity line the importer chooses the category of the goods, for example plants for planting or cut wood.
requirements.why: Policy requires the category and the goal names it. The trace slice has no category question. The list of categories is an open question with a default.

requirements.statement: For each commodity line the importer finds and adds a genus and species from reference data. They can filter the list by genus-and-species name or by EPPO code, and each entry shows its EPPO code; the notification records the EPPO code of every genus and species added. A filter with no match shows 'No search results' in the list, not an error.
requirements.why: Policy requires genus and species, and the EPPO code for plants for planting; IPAFFS captures both through one reference-data pick, so recording the pick's EPPO code satisfies the policy's EPPO requirement without a separate question. Backed by both sources. Which categories need it is an open question with a default.

requirements.statement: The importer can add more than one genus and species. Once two or more are added they can remove any of them, but they cannot remove the last one.
requirements.why: A consignment can carry several goods (policy asks for the 'relevant goods in the consignment'); IPAFFS says 'You can add multiple Genus (and Species)' and keeps at least one.

requirements.statement: Continuing without adding any genus and species shows an error and keeps the importer on the page.
requirements.why: IPAFFS requires at least one; follows from req-008. The wording is an open question with a default.

requirements.statement: For each commodity line the importer gives the quantity of the goods.
requirements.why: Policy requires the quantity and the goal names it. The trace slice does not cover quantity. What is counted, and in what unit, is an open question with a default.

requirements.statement: The data the notification captures is the policy's published 'All other goods' list, needed for risk assessment and inspection planning, and that list is only true at the time it was published.
requirements.why: Not a buildable behaviour: whether the list is current is for the policy leads to confirm. Every adopted data requirement builds to the published list meanwhile.

requirements.statement: A UK region of origin (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland) is recorded alongside the country of origin.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the policy asks for the country only, and it takes precedence over the IPAFFS behaviour.

requirements.statement: For species that carry variety and class reference data, the importer gives a variety (with a free-text 'Other' variety) and a class (Class I, Class II, Extra Class) on a Variety and class page, which sits between the genus-and-species pick and the commodity summary.
requirements.why: Out of scope: variety and class are not in the policy's data list, and the policy takes precedence over IPAFFS.

requirements.statement: A notification has a configurable maximum number of commodity lines, with advisory messages as it nears the cap and errors when it would go over.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a limit of the IPAFFS service with no basis in the policy or the goal, and the cap's value is not known. It can be added later as its own requirement.

requirements.statement: For machinery and other non-plant commodity codes, the genus-and-species step shows species as tick boxes; for a commodity with no species reference data, the step shows no species selection at all.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the goal is high-risk plants and plant products, not machinery or other objects, and both variants are IPAFFS-only behaviour never seen rendered.

requirements.statement: The chosen country of origin drives routing rules: an EU country is required when a temporary place of destination is used, and the country with the commodity decides a stored 'Article 72' low-risk classification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the goal is capturing where the goods come from and what they are, not the risk rules that act on them. The policy does not ask for these rules, and the trace itself records that what the classification changes is unknown.

requirements.statement: On the review page the country of origin has no 'Change' link, and after submission it is amended on a separate page.
requirements.why: Out of scope: review and amend journeys are not in the goal, and this IPAFFS behaviour is inferred, not observed.

requirements.statement: The notification gives the expected date the consignment lands in Great Britain or, if it has arrived, the date it first arrived.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the goal covers where the goods come from and what they are; the landing date is about the journey, not the goods. Policy alone; the trace slice does not cover it.

requirements.statement: The notification gives the consignment's intended destination or, if it has arrived there, its current location.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the goal covers where the goods come from, not where they go. Policy alone.

requirements.statement: The notification gives the name and address of the consignor.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the consignor is a party to the consignment, not a description of the goods or their origin. Policy alone.

requirements.statement: For plants for planting, the notification gives the identification number of the supplier of the plants.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the supplier id identifies a party, not what the goods are, and the goal does not list it. The EPPO code on the same policy line is adopted through req-008. Policy alone.

requirements.statement: For cut trees or trees for planting, the notification gives the size of the tree.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a category-specific extra detail the goal does not list (it names category, genus and species, commodity code and quantity). A natural next increment once categories exist. Policy alone.

requirements.statement: For wood and wood products (including isolated bark), the notification confirms what phytosanitary treatments have been applied.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a category-specific extra detail the goal does not list. Policy alone.

requirements.statement: The notification may give the intended use of the goods.
requirements.why: Out of scope: optional in the policy and not listed in the goal. Policy alone.

requirements.statement: Four wood-product and origin combinations carry additional caveats: conifer wood with bark and isolated conifer bark from an EU member state; conifer wood and isolated bark from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain; cut coniferous trees over 3 metres from an EU member state; and round or chipped wood of Fraxinus, Castanea, Juglans, Pterocarya or Platanus from an EU member state (all excluding preservative-treated wood where stated). The page does not say what the caveats require.
requirements.why: Out of scope: these are rules acting on data (origin, genus, category), not data to capture, and the page gives no obligation to build. The adopted origin, category and genus-and-species data is what a later rule would match on.
